title: Effects of prolonged choline supplementation on DNA-methylation and fat-free body mass in very preterm infants - pilot study with a dietary supplement
summary: Preterm infants still show differences in body composition and mechanisms of gene activation when compared to healthy term-born infants. One possible cause of this could be a micronutrient deficiency. Preterms have been shown to have a choline deficiency due to inadequate feeding strategies, therefore the consequences of a higher supply should be investigated.

interventions.name: 20 preterm infants (28 0/7- 31 6/7 weeks at birth) with choline-supplementation. Infants receive supplemental choline (30mg/kg/d as glycerophosphocholine) when oral feedings >100ml/kg/d are established
20 preterm infants (28 0/7- 31 6/7 weeks at birth) without choline-supplementation

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Group 1 - Preterm infants 28 0/7 - 31 6/7 gestational weeks
- Group 2 - Term-born infants >37 0/7 gestational weeks
- In case of multiple births: Only firstborn infant can be included, intervention in siblings possible if desired by the parents
Exclusion criteria:
• Malformations 
• Syndromal diseases 
• Metabolic diseases
• SGA-growth (<10P)
• Perinatal acidosis (pH <7.0)
• Neonatal Sepsis with positive blood culture or CRP >5mg/dl during the 1st week after birth
• Circulatory support (hydrocortisone or catecholamine therapy) in the first week after birth
• Gestational diabetes (with hypertrophy (>P90) or recurrent hypoglycaemia in the first days of life)
• Gastrointestinal complications (e.g. intestinal perforation) or incomplete transition to full enteral feeding until/at day 14 after birth
• Mother not willing to participate as associate
